prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Green Party Manifesto 2024 (ideological framing excluded)

Health and social care
- NHS: Additional revenue funding rising to £28bn a year by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years; £20bn for hospitals over the parliament. Reduce waiting lists, rapid GP access, same‑day urgent access, universal NHS dentistry via a new contract and investment reaching £3bn/year by 2030. Restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn), expand community diagnostics.
- Primary care: Extra funding reaching £1.5bn/year by 2030; £2bn capital; cut admin for GPs.
- Workforce: Support pay restoration (including junior doctors).
- Cancer: National plan to increase early diagnosis (75% stages 1–2 by 2028).
- Mental health: Access to evidence‑based therapies within 28 days; tailored provision; trained, paid counsellor in every school and sixth‑form college.
- Assisted dying: Support change in law with safeguards.
- HIV: End new transmissions by 2030 (PrEP access, opt‑out A&E testing).

Social care and disability
- Free personal care; £20bn/year investment; national pay, terms and career structure for care workers; visa reforms to curb exploitation.
- Disabled people: 5% uplift to disability benefits; oppose PIP vouchers; reform assessments; mandatory free transport for 16–18 SEND; workplace support.
- Children’s social care: +£3bn to local authorities; guaranteed counselling; extend staying‑put to 21.

Housing and planning
- 150,000 new social homes annually; end Right to Buy; empower rent controls; end no‑fault evictions; Private Residential Tenancy Boards; long‑term tenancies; tenants’ right to energy upgrades.
- Retrofit programme: £29bn (homes to EPC B), £4bn public buildings, £9bn low‑carbon heat, £7bn heat adaptation over five years; property‑linked finance; area‑based delivery.
- New builds: Passivhaus/equivalent; solar and low‑carbon heating mandated; whole‑life carbon assessments; reuse of demolition materials; planning oriented to public services, green space and non‑car dependence.

Energy and climate
- No new oil and gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax ramping over a decade.
- Electricity: Wind to ~70% by 2030; targets by 2035—80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar; end onshore wind barriers; Local Electricity Bill; expand grid, storage, and interconnectors; support green hydrogen.
- Community energy: Minimum community ownership thresholds; regional banks to invest.
- Nuclear: Cease new projects; plan to phase out existing.
- Skills: £4bn/year for transition training; Offshore Energy and Skills Passport.

Economy and work
- Green investment averaging £40bn/year (rail electrification, public transport, active travel, industry, water/sewage, buildings retrofit).
- Public ownership: Railways, water companies, Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Finance: Mandated fossil divestment by 2030; updated Bank of England mandate; credit guidance; FCA action on fossil equities.
- SMEs: Regional mutual banks (UKIB + £10bn); £2bn/year local grants; Prompt Payment Code in law.
- R&D: +£30bn over five years focused on climate and nature.
- Labour rights: Repeal anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15/hour minimum wage (with higher Employment Allowance); day‑one rights; gig workers classed as workers; 10:1 pay ratio cap; equal‑pay audits; move toward four‑day week.

Welfare and public finances
- Benefits: +£40/week to UC and legacy benefits; abolish five‑week wait and two‑child cap; +5% disability benefits; protect pensions; +10%/month carer’s allowance; scrap bedroom tax; end sanctions; long‑term UBI goal.
- Tax: Wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income rates with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance tax; revalue Council Tax; targeted business rate changes; higher windfall taxes; VAT shifts; carbon tax (£120/t rising toward £500/t). Estimated £50–£70bn/year extra by end of parliament; additional business and carbon revenues; borrowing to invest; savings from cancelling Trident replacement.

Nature, animals, food
- Nature: Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; increase DEFRA by £1.5bn; Right to Roam Act; peat re‑wetting; +50% unharvested woodland; £3bn/year in nature grants; urban biodiversity measures; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Animals: Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; tighter licensing and cruelty register; end factory farming practices (cages, routine antibiotics); ban snares and lead ammo.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support over five years; link payments to pesticide reduction; expand horticulture; mixed farming; reduce food waste; free school meals and breakfast clubs; strengthen supply‑chain fairness.

Education
- Early years: £1.4bn/year for Sure Start; 35 hours/week childcare from 9 months (subject to sector agreement).
- Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn teacher pay); £2.5bn/year for building safety/RAAC; curriculum breadth; Natural History GCSE; bring academies under local control; VAT on private school fees (SEND exempt).
- SEND: +£5bn for inclusive provision and transport.
- FE/HE: +£3bn for sixth forms; £12bn for skills/lifelong learning; scrap tuition fees; restore grants.

Transport
- Public transport: Subsidies to £10bn/year incl. free buses for under‑18s; +£19bn over five years for PT, electrification, cycling/walking; rail in public ownership; LA control of buses; £2.5bn/year for active travel.
- Roads/vehicles: Oppose new road building; restore fuel‑duty escalator; develop road pricing; EV scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new ICE sales by 2027 and ICE use by 2035; weight‑based VED; 20mph default in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: Frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights under 3‑hour rail alternative; no airport expansion.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Fair Politics Act: Repeal voter ID; proportional representation; state party funding; stronger transparency and oversight; votes at 16.
- Replace House of Lords with elected chamber; expand devolution; +£5bn/year to English LAs.
- Human rights: Protect HRA/ECHR; restore legal aid; repeal recent protest‑restricting laws; enable self‑ID; remove spousal veto; X gender marker option.
- Migration: End hostile environment; remove spousal income minimums; safe routes; faster asylum decisions; right to work while waiting; end NRPF and most detention; split Home Office functions; at‑cost visa fees; NHS access for visa‑holders; family reunion.

Justice and drugs
- Policing: End routine stop and search and facial recognition; strengthen accountability; diversity fitness assessments.
- Courts: +£11bn over parliament; recruit judges; repair courts.
- Crime: Presumption against custodial sentences under two years; expand diversion and restorative justice; national strategy and funding to tackle violence against women and girls; decriminalise sex work.
- Drugs: National Commission; decriminalise personal possession with health‑led diversion.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; pursue EU re‑entry (customs union first, restore free movement, rejoin Erasmus).
- Israel/Palestine: Immediate bilateral ceasefire; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; support war‑crimes investigations.
- Aid and climate finance: Raise ODA to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; support Loss and Damage; debt relief; ecocide law.
- Trade: Remove ISDS; uphold labour, animal and environmental standards.
- Security: Sign TPNW; cancel Trident and dismantle nuclear arsenal; work within NATO for no‑first‑use and defensive posture.
